_what: What tool:connect-an-account-by-signing-in-to-the-service reads (do-work/connect-by-signing-in.mjs). `routes` are its two page routes under `route_prefix` (the engine's @workshop-routes rows in trillion-rust src/server/tool-routes.json); the callback route is every switched-on descriptor's acquire.redirect.path, so the address a service sends the person back to is `public_origin` + `route_prefix` + that path. `list` is the person's service-connections list: its own choice and boolean fields are the starting values a sign-in is started with, every row it holds and every row written here is a record of type record:<its row_type>, a row of kind `sign_in_app_kind` holds a sign-in app's id in the open (an OAuth client id is not a secret, RFC 6749 section 2.2; the old Worker published it as service-plain-values) under `client_id`, named by the descriptor's hosted_client.id_name in `client_id_name`, and a connected account is a row of kind `account_kind`. `pending` is how a started sign-in waits for its callback: one record of type `type` whose id is `id_prefix` and the BLAKE3 identity of its state, until `link_seconds` (or the start's own wait_seconds) and then `state_seconds` have passed, the old Worker's LINK_SECONDS and STATE_SECONDS. `services` are the descriptors whose sign-in is switched on here: the http rows that trade the code for the tokens in order (`trade`, the first given the code), and the row that checks the new connection (`verify`, its input with `{connection_id}` standing for the new connection's id); a descriptor not named here is refused. `flows` are the descriptor acquire.flow values these routes run (the old Worker's hosted sign-in, oauth2_auth_code); a descriptor whose flow is not listed (a device code, a provider-hosted window) is refused at the start, so a new flow is one entry here and its own start and callback, never a service named in code. `words` are what the person reads; {service}, {account}, {expected} and {why} are filled in.

words.unknown_service: {service} cannot be connected by signing in here.
words.not_switched_on: Connecting {service} is not switched on yet: this account holds no sign-in app id for it. Nothing was sent anywhere.
words.starting_value: Say each starting value of the new connection: {why}.
words.bad_scopes: scopes must name only scopes this service's sign-in lists, separated by spaces or commas: {why}.
words.bad_wait: wait_seconds must be a whole number of seconds above 0.
words.bad_return: return_to must be a path on this site that starts with one /.
words.expired: This sign-in has expired or was already used. Nothing was saved. Ask for a new link to connect.
words.not_connected: {service} was not connected: the sign-in was cancelled, refused, or no longer matches this service. Nothing was saved. Ask for a new link to try again.
words.refused: {service} was not connected: {why} Nothing was saved. Ask for a new link to try again.
words.no_token: the service answered without a token.
words.not_checked: the new connection could not be checked with the service.
words.no_account: this sign-in does not reach any account Trillion can connect.
words.many_accounts: this sign-in reaches more than one account; connect again and pick just one on the sign-in page.
words.other_account: you signed in as {account}, and this link was made for {expected}. Sign in with {expected}.
words.unnamed_account: the service did not say which account signed in, so it could not be checked against {expected}.
words.connected: {service} is connected as {account}. Your AI can use it now. You can close this tab.
words.connected_back: {service} is connected as {account}. Your AI can use it now. Go back: {back}
